task: Independent read-only Windows native script TOML boot timeout diagnosis
executed_checks: NONE: no source changes, native test runs, workflow reruns, HTTP/network, reference/JVM, guard/upload or signing controls.
findings: API [api] bind=127.0.0.1:0 is correct and resolves through actual listener local_addr before api_addr publication. P2P bind key is [peers] bind_addr; absent disables inbound, so original test has no default9030 bind collision.

NodeConfig::load defaults mainnet and appends13 public bootstrap seeds after the configured127.0.0.1:1. common::make_test_config instead constructs only unreachable loopback. Original test is consequently not isolated from ordinary outbound attempts/background sync; causal relation to this timeout is not proved.

Top-level network=devnet selects an empty seed list; known loopback peer remains valid. Explicit [peers] bind_addr=127.0.0.1:0 is accepted and adds an ephemeral inbound listener; omit/empty keeps outbound-only.

CLI ibd_flush_interval defaults500 (not a TOML field); common test uses0. Fresh UTXO boot initializes genesis before enabling the64-job persist worker. Policy routes do not wait for a future full-block durable commit, and no persistence deadlock is established.

All seven script POST routes share outer Tier::Operator auth selected by config.api_script.require_api_key. API boot copies config to ServerCtx, then ScriptState, and mounts all seven. Missing key responds401 before JSON parsing/governor. Valid key plusJSON{} has the exact statuses/reasons listed; bare404/500/429/503 or a noncanonical401 must not satisfy the positive assertion.

API server delegates to axum0.7.9/hyper1.9.0 without a custom connection-lifetime gate. Hyper parses Connection:close to disabled keep-alive, closes after body/response completion, and polls socket shutdown. Middleware rejection of an unread tiny body is drained or closed rather than requiring node shutdown.

Windows receipt only records Elapsed at read_to_end timeout line600 and a9.48-second test total. It does not record route, key case, status headers, byte count or partial response. Therefore it cannot distinguish delayed admission/body from complete response awaiting FIN and cannot establish or rule out a production transport issue.

Reading a protocol-framed response under a bounded meaningful test deadline, checking exact HTTP status plus JSON reason/detail, and reporting route/key/partial bytes on failures directly tests auth policy without making EOF timing its assertion. Isolation removes unrelated public outbound work. This is a recommended test-contract repair, not proof of the physical Windows cause.
